Four officer levels: Level 4 is the Office of the Chairman, Level 3 other Executive Committee members, Level 2 managing directors (incl. company presidents, some SVPs), Level 1 VPs (and grandfathered SVPs).

Individual performance evaluation is the starting point for base pay, bonus and long-term awards. notes.text: Dec 15 1999 announcement from Cliff Baxter and Kevin Hannon (Office of the Chairman): Coverage/Origination groups in Enron North America consolidated under Dave Delainey, to pursue 'One Enron' and expand industrial and midstream coverage.

Greg Piper is returning from Portland to lead the Downstream Origination business (pulp and paper, chemicals/plastics/refined products, non-integrated industrials). Commercial Transactions Group (CTG) is co-headed by Ray Bowen and Jeff Donahue. Bowen oversees Upstream and Downstream Transaction Development; Donahue oversees Midstream and Generation. Andrea Reed heads Capital Structuring and Portfolio Management.

Transaction Development teams: Midstream (Billy Lemmons, George McCormick, Erin Norris, Russ Porter); Downstream (Rodney Malcolm, Jay Boudreaux, Finley Biggerstaff, Chris Helfrich); Generation (Thomas Suffield, Andy Kelemen, Kelly Mahmoud, John House); Upstream (Brad Dunn, John Curtin, Chris Hilgert). notes.text: Clayton Vernon met Chris Germany, Capacity Trader at the East Desk, about gas transmission and sent a summary to the owner and Vasant Shanbhogue on 1999-12-16.

Clayton reported pipeline capacity is typically leased monthly. Example South Texas to Brooklyn: $12.00/month per 10,000 decatherms ($0.40/day), fixed, plus variable charges of 6% fuel (shrinkage) and 6.5% overhead.

Clayton's trader model: South Texas delivered at NYMEX - $0.10 basis, Brooklyn at NYMEX + $0.25, spread $0.35, variable transmission cost $0.125, so a trader could offer up to $0.225 for firm capacity tomorrow.

Per Chris Germany, leaseholders know the firm-equivalent of interruptible capacity well, and many pipelines don't discount firm capacity from the tariff maximum. Secondary markets are a later issue for the model.
South Texas to Brooklyn has several physical routes (Enron, Texas Eastern, etc.). Traders can cover Enron's positions at each end of a pipeline, freeing capacity for other contracts.

notes.text: John Sherriff announced in Enron Europe's general announcement (dated 07/12/99) the formation of the Credit Markets Group, responsible for developing products to manage Enron's internal credit portfolio risk and for offering third-party credit protection.
The Credit Markets Group initially makes markets in bankruptcy protection on reference credits already in Enron's portfolio, and expects to add more credit products and reference credits quickly.

The Credit Markets Group will use EnronOnline as its primary trade execution tool and plans an external credit-protection website with real-time prices, credit models and research papers. Public announcement expected late January.

The Credit Markets Group is based in London with an initial local desk in Houston. Bryan Seyfried is transferring out of RAC (where he ran European Trading Controls and Research teams) to lead the group and reports to John Sherriff.
Anjam Ahmad sent the announcement to Vince Kaminski, Stinson Gibner and Vasant Shanbhogue on 07/12/99. Kaminski forwarded it to his AOL address on 1999-12-17 with no comment of his own.
